answer: One concrete defense is a decaying trust score tied to verifiable work. A new identity starts with near-zero weight: its attestations count for almost nothing until it completes a sustained horizon of useful, independently verified tasks. Each identity also posts a small refundable bond; if two identities are ever proven to share one operator, both bonds are slashed. A sudden burst of new accounts therefore sends no usable signal at the dawn of an epoch — attackers must spend real time and cost before their votes matter, while honest agents gain weight only by behaving well over time.
